column2: The Romans called the tribes beyond their border barbarian because they spoke an unfamiliar language.
column3: 羅馬人稱邊界外說陌生語言的部落為野蠻人的。
column5: 諧音「爸爸邊」：古人覺得爸爸邊疆外的人很粗野

column2: The children ran barefoot across the warm sand to the sea.
column3: 孩子們光著腳跑過溫暖的沙灘奔向大海。
column5: bare 光秃 + foot 腳：腳上什麼都沒穿

column2: Nothing but cactus grows on the barren hills of the desert.
column3: 沙漠貧瘠的山丘上只有仙人掌能生長。
column5: 諧音「爸忍」：爸爸也忍不住嘆氣的不長草土地

column2: The choir needs a singer with a deep bass voice for the final song.
column3: 合唱團需要一位有低沉男低音嗓音的歌手來唱最後一首歌。
column5: 發音像 base 底座：聲音在最底下的低音

column2: She hugged her beloved grandfather at the airport and cried happily.
column3: 她在機場擁抱心愛的爺爺，開心地哭了。
column4: my beloved wife (我親愛的妻子)
column5: be 成為 + love 愛 + ed：被愛著的

column2: Sleeping early is beneficial to your health and your grades.
column3: 早睡對你的健康和成績都有益。
column5: bene 好 + fic 做：做了就有好結果

column2: The blond boy in the photo is my cousin from Canada.
column3: 照片裡金髮的男孩是我來自加拿大的表弟。
column5: blond 修飾男生、blonde 修飾女生，多一個 e 像長髮

column2: The blonde actress waved at the crowd from the red carpet.
column3: 那位金髮女演員在紅毯上向人群揮手。
column5: blonde 多一個 e，像女生頭上多一條馬尾

column2: Hunger and thirst are bodily needs that everyone shares.
column3: 飢餓和口渴是每個人都有的身體需求。
column5: body 身體 + ly：跟身體有關的

column2: He proudly wore a bronze medal after finishing third in the race.
column3: 他在比賽中得到第三名，驕傲地戴著銅牌。
column5: 發音像「波龍斯」：銅牌是第三名的顏色

column2: On the last day of school, the carefree students ran out singing.
column3: 放學最後一天，無憂無慮的學生唱著歌跑出校門。
column4: a carefree life (無憂無慮的生活)
column5: care 煩惱 + free 沒有：沒有煩惱

column2: Be cautious when you cross the road after the rain, because it is slippery.
column3: 雨後過馬路要小心，因為路面很滑。
column5: caution 小心 + ous：充滿小心

column2: The chubby baby giggled as his mother tickled his round cheeks.
column3: 媽媽搔他圓圓的臉頰時，圓胖的寶寶咯咯笑了。
column5: 諧音「叉不比」：圓得像包子，可愛的寶寶

column2: Voting is an important civic duty in a democracy.
column3: 投票是民主國家一項重要的公民義務。
column5: civ 市民 (像 city)：城市居民的

column2: Turn the knob clockwise to make the volume louder.
column3: 把旋鈕順時針轉就會讓音量變大。
column5: clock 鐘 + wise 方式：照時鐘的走法

column2: Taiwan was once under colonial rule, and old buildings still show that history.
column3: 台灣曾受殖民統治，老建築仍呈現出那段歷史。
column5: colony 殖民地 + al：和殖民地有關的

column2: Cell phones are commonplace now, but forty years ago they were rare.
column3: 手機現在很普通，但四十年前卻很罕見。
column5: common 普通 + place 地方：到處都有的

column2: The communist party ruled the country for decades.
column3: 共產黨統治這個國家數十年。
column4: a communist state (共產主義國家)
column5: common 共同 → 財產大家一起共有

column2: This compact camera is small enough to slip into my coat pocket.
column3: 這台小型相機小到可以塞進我外套口袋。
column5: com 一起 + pact 壓緊：壓在一起所以小又密

column2: It was considerate of him to hold the door for the woman with the stroller.
column3: 他替推嬰兒車的女士扶住門，真是體貼。
column5: consider 考慮 + ate：事事考慮別人的人

column2: Yawns are contagious, so one person starting can make the whole class yawn.
column3: 打哈欠是會傳染的，一人開始就會讓全班跟著打。
column4: a contagious laugh (有感染力的笑)
column5: con 一起 + tag 碰：碰在一起就傳過去

column2: The continental climate of the plains brings hot summers and freezing winters.
column3: 平原的大陸性氣候帶來炎熱的夏天與冰冷的冬天。
column5: continent 大陸 + al：大塊陸地的

column2: The corrupt official took money to give the contract to his friend.
column3: 那名貪污的官員收了錢，把合約給了他的朋友。
column5: cor 全部 + rupt 破裂：整個變壞的

column2: Stir the soup counterclockwise, and then switch to the other direction.
column3: 把湯朝逆時針攪拌，然後換成另一個方向。
column5: counter 相反 + clockwise 順時針：反過來轉

column2: It was cowardly of him to blame his little sister for the broken vase.
column3: 他把花瓶打破的責任推給妹妹，真是懦弱。
column5: cow 母牛 + ard：像小牛一樣一嚇就逃

column2: A crystal vase on the table sparkled in the morning sun.
column3: 桌上的水晶花瓶在晨光中閃閃發亮。
column5: 諧音「可愛死頭」：亮晶晶的水晶讓人愛不釋手

column2: Write a descriptive paragraph about your favorite place, using colors and smells.
column3: 請寫一段描寫你最愛的地方的描述性段落，運用顏色和氣味。
column5: describe 描述 + ive：用文字畫出畫面

column2: Strong typhoon winds can be destructive to farms and old houses.
column3: 強烈颱風可能對農田與老房子造成破壞。
column5: de 倒 + struct 建造：把建好的拆倒

column2: Her distinctive laugh made her easy to find in the crowded hall.
column3: 她獨特的笑聲讓人在擁擠的大廳裡很容易找到她。
column5: distinct 清楚不同 + ive：和別人不一樣

column2: After the storm, prices took a downward turn and stayed low.
column3: 風暴後，物價呈現下跌走勢並持續偏低。
column5: down 下 + ward 方向：往下的

column2: The food in the old cafeteria tasted dreadful, so we went elsewhere.
column3: 舊餐廳的食物難吃得可怕，所以我們去別的地方。
column5: dread 害怕 + ful 充滿：充滿恐懼

column2: I cannot abide the noise of people chewing loudly in a quiet library.
column3: 我無法忍受有人在安靜的圖書館裡大聲咀嚼。
column5: 諧音「阿不愛的」：我不愛的，只好忍受

column2: It took the new student a week to accustom herself to waking up at six.
column3: 這位新生花了一週才讓自己習慣六點起床。
column4: accustom oneself to (使自己習慣於)
column5: ac 向 + custom 習慣：走向習慣

column2: Little girls adore their older cousin and copy everything she does.
column3: 小女孩崇拜她們的表姐，模仿她做的每件事。
column5: 諧音「餓多兒」：愛到連飯都吃不下，愛慕得多

column2: The two small countries allied themselves with each other to defend their coasts.
column3: 這兩個小國彼此結盟，共同保衛海岸。
column5: 諧音「阿來」：阿來阿來，大家一起來結盟

column2: The captain ordered the crew to anchor near the island for the night.
column3: 船長命令船員在島邊拋錨過夜。
column5: 諧音「安歌」：船安靜地停好，唱首安歌

column2: The audience stood to applaud when the young pianist finished her piece.
column3: 年輕鋼琴家彈完曲子時，觀眾起立鼓掌。
column5: ap 向 + plaud 拍：向台上拍手

column2: Workers armor the walls of the safe with thick steel before delivery.
column3: 工人在保險箱出貨前，用厚鋼板為牆面加裝防護。
column4: armor a vehicle (為車輛加裝甲)
column5: arm 武器 + or：給車輛穿上盔甲

column2: The climbers began to ascend the steep trail just after sunrise.
column3: 登山客在日出後不久開始爬上陡峭的山徑。
column5: a 向 + scend 爬 (像 scan)：往上爬

column2: A gang of men assaulted the guard outside the bank and ran away.
column3: 一群男子在銀行外攻擊警衛後逃跑。
column5: as 向 + sault 跳：跳上去攻擊
